g.title: Admit explicit recovery; Engineering command interface (MOD-010); Validate selectors and the closed complete/restore action before dispatching the exact recovery request to executeRecordStore.

Validate retained journal; Operational record persistence (MOD-011); Before exclusion, load the expected journal bytes and verify their digest, transaction/change identity, canonical encoding, supported version and prepared/committed phase, snapshot content hashes, scope, preservation, write/read sets, and tracked directory identities.

Acquire recovery exclusion; Operational record persistence (MOD-011); Reject a live competing lock owner. Remove an exactly observed stale owner lock when admitted, exclusively acquire a new owned lock, and update the epoch. Private coordination effects are distinct from authoritative recovery.

Recheck recovery admissibility; Operational record persistence (MOD-011); Reload the exact expected journal under exclusion and require every observed target to equal its retained before or candidate identity, including absence. A committed journal requires candidate identities and rejects restore; it cannot authorize rollback.
The requested action is restore and the verified journal is prepared.

Prepare before-state recovery receipt; Operational record persistence (MOD-011); Prepare and validate the recovered result against the exact retained before-set before touching authoritative files. Restoration does not require external read-basis files to retain their old values and never writes those files.

Restore exact retained before bytes; Operational record persistence (MOD-011); Publish the retained before-set with repeated exclusion, containment, and known-state checks. Remove only permitted transaction-created files and tracked empty directories; do not overwrite an observed third state or unrelated content.

Finish verified restoration; Operational record persistence (MOD-011); Verify the terminal before identities, remove the retained journal, release owned exclusion, and return the prepared recovered receipt. Failure at any point preserves an explicit incomplete/unknown outcome for reinspection.
Return recovered for the verified exact before-state only after successful restoration and cleanup. No workflow decision, replay, or blanket project rollback is performed.

Prepare candidate recovery receipt; Operational record persistence (MOD-011); For complete, verify the retained declared read basis and prepare/validate a recovered result against the exact retained candidate before authoritative writes. The advanced recovery result is prepared within Store.prepareResult.

Complete exact retained candidate; Operational record persistence (MOD-011); Publish the retained candidate with repeated owned-lock, path, target before/candidate, and decision-basis checks. A committed journal permits only candidate bytes; unknown values stop completion.

Recheck basis and commit recovery; Operational record persistence (MOD-011); Recheck declared reads after candidate publication. For a prepared journal, observed basis drift attempts guarded restoration before reporting failure. Otherwise persist phase=committed; a previously committed journal is never rolled back.

Finish verified completion; Operational record persistence (MOD-011); Remove the verified terminal journal, release the owned lock, and return the prepared recovered result. Interrupted cleanup or a subsequent failure requires reinspection with the current recovery identity.
Return recovered for the exact retained candidate after verified completion and cleanup. The result proves no new engineering decision, requirement satisfaction, or successful output delivery.

text.tspan: See the recorded conditions and effects below

g.title:
A selected journal, snapshot, target, action, version, or identity is missing, changed, incompatible, or untrusted; a target matches neither retained side. Stop recovery without guessing state or replaying actor intent. The advanced wrapper reports recovery-required, except a live writer is busy. Checks made before exclusion produce no recovery writes; later rejection may follow private lock/epoch effects. Missing recovery metadata is reported as unavailable, not invented.; A committed journal with an observed before-state target is inconsistent and rejected. Restore is rejected even when a committed journal otherwise validates.
Completion observes changed declared read basis, or a restore/complete filesystem operation or cleanup is interrupted. Keep the actual incomplete or uncertain recovery outcome explicit; reinspection and an explicitly selected current recovery identity are required. Before committed phase, the source may attempt exact guarded restoration after post-publication basis drift. That attempt is not a guarantee that all previous bytes were restored.; After committed phase, no recovery path restores before bytes. Retained evidence and known target identities govern completion/cleanup, not a blind retry.
